direction_signature.conclusion: There is a real but narrow signature: these figures make the input/history itself a manipulable, ordered object—then visualize controlled disclosure, placement, or external memory around it. Generic ML mechanism figures can use boxes and arrows too; they usually do not make a text history's order, length, and recoverability the visual object of study.

claims.claim: Ordered conversation is rendered as turn-indexed speech or message units, usually with time or session structure, in 10 figures: 2505.06120-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn-conversation/00-LIC_Teaser.png, 2505.06120-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn-conversation/02-LIC_Conv_Types_v3.png, 2410.10813-longmemeval-benchmarking-chat-assistants-on/00-main_examples.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/00-intro_figure_conv_only_v2.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/02-main_v4.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/07-summary_prompt_arxiv.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/08-observation_prompt_arxiv.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/10-conv_edits.png, 2310.08560-memgpt-towards-llms-as-operating-systems/00-memgpt_diagrams_wide_memory_creation.png, and 2310.08560-memgpt-towards-llms-as-operating-systems/01-memgpt_diagrams_wide_memory_search.png. This is distinctive because chronological language interaction is the mechanism, not just an input example.

Controlled disclosure or position within a long text is made visible as colored shards, document order, or a marked context strip in 8 figures: 2505.06120-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn-conversation/01-LIC_simulator_flat_v3.png, 2505.06120-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn-conversation/02-LIC_Conv_Types_v3.png, 2505.06120-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn-conversation/03-LIC_Tasks_v2.png, 2502.05167-nolima-long-context-evaluation-beyond-litera/09-full_vs_last2K_demonstration.png, 2502.05167-nolima-long-context-evaluation-beyond-litera/10-HaystackPipeline.png, 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/01-qa_example.png, 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/02-qa_changing_position.png, and 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/03-qa_changing_length.png. This is the clearest visual signature of evaluation work that treats ordering and length as causal interventions.

Externalized memory is shown as an operational state boundary—write, search, then overwrite/reconcile—in 4 figures: 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/02-main_v4.png, 2310.08560-memgpt-towards-llms-as-operating-systems/00-memgpt_diagrams_wide_memory_creation.png, 2310.08560-memgpt-towards-llms-as-operating-systems/01-memgpt_diagrams_wide_memory_search.png, and 2310.08560-memgpt-towards-llms-as-operating-systems/02-memgpt_diagrams_wide_memory_correction.png. It is a convention in this packet, but not a majority pattern.

Verbatim prompts and source text are retained as evidence rather than abstracted away in 9 figures: 2505.06120-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn-conversation/03-LIC_Tasks_v2.png, 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/01-qa_example.png, 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/02-qa_changing_position.png, 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/03-qa_changing_length.png, 2307.03172-lost-in-the-middle-how-language-models-use-l/05-kv_retrieval_example.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/04-persona_appendix.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/05-event_prompts_appendix.png, 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/07-summary_prompt_arxiv.png, and 2402.17753-evaluating-very-long-term-conversational-mem/08-observation_prompt_arxiv.png. The mechanism must stay auditably linguistic.

A single explicit long-context bar with needle ticks is anecdotal (2 figures): 2502.05167-nolima-long-context-evaluation-beyond-litera/09-full_vs_last2K_demonstration.png and 2502.05167-nolima-long-context-evaluation-beyond-litera/10-HaystackPipeline.png; it is not a packet-wide convention.

how_the_haystack_is_drawn.drawing: A horizontal stream of colored shard cards is revealed one shard at a time through the simulator stages.
A blue full-instruction bar becomes small yellow blocks; rows indexed by turn place those blocks at different disclosure times.
Each task shows a blue/grey full instruction above a row of short yellow sharded-instruction boxes.
History is a vertical stack of colored chat bubbles grouped into single-session and cross-session examples.
Evidence sessions are mini chat transcripts; their history construction is shown as several boxed sessions converging into a released chat history.
Long context is a long grey-and-blue horizontal bar, with thin red vertical needle markers; full and last-2K policies are separate stacked lanes.
The haystack is a tall scrolling document/page glyph with many grey text lines; retained or inserted evidence is highlighted in orange.
The context is a verbatim prompt box containing numbered documents; the answer-bearing document is bolded.
The context is a verbatim numbered-document prompt whose answer document is moved to a different ordinal position.
The context is a verbatim numbered-document prompt with extra irrelevant documents inserted around the bold answer document.
The context is a dense verbatim JSON-like key-value list inside a prompt box, with the relevant record emphasized.
Conversation history is a vertical chain of alternating blue and grey speech bubbles; side labels and curved arrows point to earlier persona and event facts.
An original session is a stack of small document/chat blocks feeding an agent; separate long-term-memory, observation, and reflection boxes represent compressed or retrieved history.
The history is shown as an input-conversation column of chat bubbles next to a generated response; the rest of the figure plots history-length effects.
History is abstracted into a horizontal dated timeline of event cards with causal connectors, rather than shown as raw dialogue.
A verbatim session log is stacked as alternating chat bubbles beside a dense generated summary; the preceding summary is shown as a separate prompt field.
A verbatim conversation is a stacked dialogue panel, paired with a right-side observations list extracted from it.
The history is a short chat thread in before/after editorial lanes, with removed and revised turns marked by red/green symbols.
The active context is alternating chat bubbles; black code-like memory-write boxes visibly append durable facts after a context-pressure alert.
The live chat is overlaid by a dark recall-store search panel listing dated past snippets, then resumes with the retrieved fact.
A short chat is paired with a dark working-context replacement command, making a memory edit visible as a before/after state change.
